speaker: n
text: There once was a hero who saved the world.

speaker: n
text: He had saved it so many times that, somewhere along the way, he started putting the world above himself.

speaker: n
text: Today was routine. A runaway car. A gasp from the crowd. A save.

speaker: crowd
text: HOORAY! Thank you, Hero!

speaker: n
text: And when the applause comes, he knows it is time to leave.

speaker: n
text: On his way home, his wrist starts beeping.

speaker: n
text: Another crime in progress.

speaker: n
text: So he turns around, to save the day again.

speaker: hero
text: Hey, criminals. You know what to do.

speaker: n
text: And they do. They drop their weapons and shuffle toward him, sadly.

speaker: n
text: The cops arrive. The hero waits, arms crossed, tapping his foot.

speaker: hero
text: So... do you guys have this?

speaker: cop
text: Almost. Let's wait for the paddy wagon.

speaker: n
text: So the hero stands there, staring off into the distance.

speaker: n
text: And he starts to think about his life.

speaker: th
text: I do all these things... but who am I doing them for?

speaker: th
text: For the world. Obviously.

speaker: th
text: But what does the world mean... for me?

speaker: n
text: He knows he should be happy. He knows he should feel satisfied, saving the world every day.

speaker: n
text: But when he looks at the criminals...

speaker: n
text: ...at the cop...

speaker: n
text: ...at the paddy wagon, stuck in traffic...

speaker: n
text: ...he feels an emptiness inside him.

speaker: n
text: Something he cannot say out loud. Something he can't tell anyone.

speaker: th
text: Because if I did... what would happen?

speaker: n
text: Back home, he posts his daily gratitude message on the newspaper's website.

speaker: n
text: Then he tucks himself into bed.

speaker: n
text: He stares at the ceiling. He looks around his house...

speaker: n
text: ...at himself, smiling, in all the newspaper pictures on the wall.

speaker: n
text: And he realizes that he has lost himself.

speaker: th
text: If I take a break, people will suffer.

speaker: th
text: If I don't take a break... I suffer.

speaker: th
text: What can I do?

speaker: n
text: Then he sees someone moving in the shadows.

speaker: th
text: Who's dumb enough to break into MY house?

speaker: th
text: ...Eh. Let them grab what they want. I'll grab them later.

speaker: th
text: I just need some rest.

speaker: n
text: And he drifts off to sleep.

speaker: n
text: But then he's woken up... by somebody poking him in the forehead.

speaker: hero
text: ...What do you want, buddy?

speaker: crim
text: I'm here to steal your stuff. And you're not going to do anything?

speaker: hero
text: No. I don't feel like doing anything.

speaker: crim
text: Hey, buddy. What's going on here? Aren't you supposed to be the one who saves the day?

speaker: hero
text: I do save the day. But it's harder to save the days now...

speaker: hero
text: ...and I barely even want to save myself anymore.

speaker: crim
text: Look here, buddy. You can't just let me walk around here stealing stuff. Where's your self-respect?

speaker: hero
text: Do you want me to put you in prison or something?

speaker: crim
text: No! I love stealing things. I'm just surprised to see the hero lying in bed while his home gets ransacked.

speaker: hero
text: Take what you want. I can get it all back later. It means nothing to me.

speaker: crim
text: So your stuff has no meaning to you?

speaker: crim
text: Do the people you save have no meaning to you?

speaker: crim
text: Do YOU have no meaning to yourself?

speaker: hero
text: I just do what I must. Who cares about me? I'm here to serve the people.

speaker: crim
text: If you can't serve yourself, by caring for yourself and listening to your heart...

speaker: crim
text: ...then maybe the weight of the world is a burden, and not a gift.

speaker: hero
text: What are you, a therapist or something now?

speaker: crim
text: No. I'm no therapist.

speaker: crim
text: But when I see the hero, the main character of the story, putting his own needs in the gutter... no wonder you feel like you're in the gutter.

speaker: crim
text: Everyone pats you on the back. But do they really? Or do they thank you for what you do, and never help, so you can help yourself?

speaker: hero
text: Look, just take what you want. Call it payment for the therapy session.

speaker: crim
text: I don't want your stuff. It doesn't mean anything to you, so it doesn't mean anything to me.

speaker: crim
text: I feel like I am stealing from someone who has bigger problems than me.

speaker: crim
text: But I'll take this money right here. Call it a consolation prize.

speaker: hero
text: What the actual f*** just happened?

speaker: hero
text: Did a criminal just feel so bad for me that he put back everything he stole?

speaker: n
text: So the hero goes back to saving the day.

speaker: n
text: At the next crime scene, the criminals look at him. But they aren't scowling this time.

speaker: n
text: They look at him with sadness. Not for themselves. For him.

speaker: n
text: He sees it, just for a moment. Then he shakes his head, and thinks nothing of it.

speaker: n
text: One day, he flies over the prison, making sure everything is in order.

speaker: n
text: He sees a guard beating a prisoner. And on the prisoner's face, a look of hate.

speaker: n
text: The hero shakes his head, and thinks nothing of it.

speaker: n
text: So he returns home again, and tucks himself in.

speaker: n
text: He opens one eye... and there's the criminal, leaning against the wall, arms crossed, looking at the trophies.

speaker: hero
text: Are you looking to steal one of those?

speaker: crim
text: No. I'm just wondering what you think of them.

speaker: hero
text: They are nice. They show that what I have done has meaning.

speaker: hero
text: Wait. Aren't you going to give me some more therapy or something?

speaker: crim
text: No. Won't the trophies keep you company?

speaker: hero
text: Well, just get out of here, then.

speaker: crim
text: I will. Have fun with your trophies.

speaker: hero
text: I WILL.

speaker: n
text: He looks at the trophies... and feels nothing.

speaker: th
text: What does any of this even mean?

speaker: n
text: Outside, the criminal watches him through the window. Then he puts his head down, and walks away.

speaker: n
text: The next night, the criminal comes back. The door is unlocked.

speaker: hero
text: Watch out, you fiend! I will not let you steal my valuables!

speaker: crim
text: Oh, why would I want to steal this junk?

speaker: hero
text: Junk?! That's not junk! Those things are VALUABLE!

speaker: crim
text: Oh yeah? If they're so valuable... watch this.

speaker: n
text: Then the criminal picks up a picture of the hero with his adopted mom...

speaker: n
text: ...and sees the sad look in the hero's eye.

speaker: n
text: The hero sees it, and has to turn away... as the clock bounces off his head.

speaker: crim
text: Well, uhh... I think I have all of the goods I need. I'll, uh, get going now.

speaker: n
text: The hero stands there, frozen, head down, with his back turned to the criminal.

speaker: n
text: So the criminal keeps coming back, here and there, to steal. And every time, the hero stops him and sends him on his way.

speaker: hero
text: Wait. You forgot to take something.

speaker: crim
text: Maybe I don't need to take anything anymore.

speaker: hero
text: W-what do you mean?

speaker: crim
text: Well, why would I want to take anything from you anymore?

speaker: hero
text: Because... you're a criminal?

speaker: crim
text: But am I still a criminal?

speaker: hero
text: ...Just leave.

speaker: crim
text: Make me.

speaker: n
text: The hero thinks about pulling him off. But his arms relax, and he says nothing.

speaker: crim
text: Well... see you later.
